task.title: Organize service account access by group
task.shortdesc: The Organization Administrator can create a new User Access group with roles or permissions that are specific to a service account. This group has the permissions that allow a service account to access services and applications on the Red Hat Hybrid Cloud Console.

prereq.note: Any user can create a service account but only the Organization Administrator or a User Access administrator can create a new group for a service account.

ul.li: Ensure you are logged in to the Red Hat Hybrid Cloud Console as an Organization Administrator or as a user with User Access administrator permissions.
Confirm one or more service accounts are associated with your Red Hat organization account.
Ensure you have access to the saved Client Secret information for the service account that you add to the User Access group.

prereq.note: The Client Secret information is displayed once when you create a new service account. You must copy and save that information. It is not displayed again.

context.p: In this example, you create a group that allows a service account to view automation analytics on the Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform.

step.cmd: From the Red Hat Hybrid Cloud Console, click the settings icon (⚙) and click User Access.
Click the Groups tab and click Create Group.
Add a Group name and a Group description. The description is optional.
Click Next to add roles to the group. For this example, find Automation Analytics viewer and click the checkbox next to the role name.
Click Next to display Add members. Because you are adding a service account and not a member, click Next.
Add service accounts appears. Choose the service account you want to add and click the checkbox next to the name.
Click Next and review the details. If no changes are needed, click Submit. The new group is created that contains the service account and the Automation Analytics viewer role and permissions.
